entries.en: Commander. You have a minute to talk?
All right.
I figured since the crew was so small, you might be more permissive.
I mean, that helmsman of yours. Most places, he'd be at captain's mast every day.
No, sir. Well, maybe.
I know things are different aboard the Normandy, but-- I'm concerned about the aliens. Vakarian and Wrex.
I know things are different aboard the Normandy, but-- I'm concerned about the turian. Vakarian.
I know things are different aboard the Normandy, but-- I'm concerned about the krogan. Wrex.
With all due respect, Commander, should they have full access to the ship?
With all due respect, Commander, should he have full access to the ship?
This is the most advanced ship in the Alliance Navy.
I don't think we should give them free reign to poke around the vital systems.
I don't think we should give him free reign to poke around the vital systems.
Engines. Sensors. Weapons.
I'm not sure I'd call the Council races allies.
I'm not sure I'd call the krogan allies.
Sir! No, sir!
I'm sorry. I was out of line. I'll get back to my duties, Commander.
Under orders to let aliens gather military intelligence? I can't believe that was the Alliance's intention.
I'd be more comfortable if they didn't have access to engineering and the CIC.
We--humanity, I mean--have to learn to rely on ourselves.
I don't think we should turn down allies. I just think we shouldn't bet everything on them staying allies.
No, sir! That's patriotism.
I don't mean we should mistreat them, Commander. I just think we should be prepared to go it without them.
As noble as the Council members seem now, if their backs are against the wall, they'll abandon us.
A pessimist is what an optimist calls a realist.
I don't think it's a grudge. I think it's--
Look. If you're fighting a bear, and the only way for you to survive is to sic your dog on it and run, you'll do it. As much as you love your dog, it isn't human.
It's not racism. Not really. Members of their species will always be more important to them than humans are.
My family's defended the Alliance since it was founded.
Terra Firma is a pack of jackals. The founders had ideals. These days they just play off xenophobia and bigotry.
I hope my reasons are more rational.
My father, grandfather, great-grandmother -- they all picked up a rifle and swore the Oath of Service.
I guess we just tend to think of Earth's interests as our own.
Couldn't say, Commander.
We probably have a lot in common. You join up to carry on the tradition?
You're lucky. I spent most of my career as groundside garrison.
I read about Mindoir. The Alliance screwed the pooch on that one. Should have had a bigger garrison.
Is that why you're out here? To take the fight to the pirates?
Amen to that.
So why are you out here? Just trying to get away from Earth?
Glad to hear it. I'd hate to think you're out here for a free college education.
Yeah. I still remember my first field exercise on Titan.
When we hit mud, the reality hit me: "I'm the first person who's ever stood here."
Then my drill instructor kicked me in the ass. I went face-first into the muck. He spent the next five minutes chewing me out for "goldbricking."
Oh, Lord. You went to the Macapá boot camp too?
Yeah, Gunny Ellison's still reaming out recruits down there. Kicking ass and using words like "inveigle" and "pusillanimous."
Most satisfying part of the job, Commander.
But right now, it's not the best place to be. I guess without a family, you had no reason to stay.
No, sir.
I did get a rotation on a space station for training. "Every marine, a rifleman; every rifleman, zee-gee certified."
I-- No, sir!
Anyway, that's why I haven't served with many aliens, Commander.
Aye, aye, Commander.
It won't be a problem, Commander. You say "jump," I say "how high." You tell me to kiss a turian, I'll ask which cheek.
You never know, Commander.
That depends, sir. If you ordered me to kiss a superior officer, that would be a violation of the regs concerning fraternization.
That would make it an illegal order. I'd be required to decline, and relieve you of command.
Sir.
Anything else you need, Commander?
--Oh, before I go. You said you're serving with Commander Shepard now? We saw him on the news here. He's cute. Later, sis.
Tell me you didn't hear that.
Oh, shoot me now.
One of my sisters.
Uh, I should be inspecting my firearm.
No, sir. You don't.
Sorry about that. It won't happen again.
Until I get home and kill her.
That's Sarah. The youngest.
Surprised to see you here, sir. Thought you'd be chatting up what's-her-name. T'Soni.
It's not. I just thought we were getting along pretty well. Sir.
No worries, sir. Probably for the best anyway. The regs frown on fraternization.
I read you, sir.
I won't keep you any more. Have fun. Commander.
Hmm. All right. But I'm the jealous type, Commander. Just so you know.
Scuttlebutt says you've got a bit of thing for her.
I could understand why. The crew's off-limits, with the regs against fraternization. And at least she looks like a woman.
So you are interested in her.
'Course, it could just be politics. Alien diplomat's daughter? Us under orders to make nice with the bug-eyed monsters?
What's up? You didn't come by to eavesdrop on family mail.
Sorry, Commander. Too much in the family mindset. My sisters and I have always been close.
Yeah, we've always been close. Me and my sisters, especially.
With Dad on duty so much, I had to help Mom raise them.
Yeah. I'm the oldest, then Abby, then Lynn. Sarah's the youngest. She's still in high school.
With four girls, Dad used to say he felt more outnumbered at home than on maneuvers.
Yeah. Took any crap posting he could get that offered space time.
He worked his ass off trying to get recognized. But he never got above Serviceman Third Class.
I hope we can get the Council to give us a hand, skipper.
Alenko-- the lieutenant. I'd hate to think his loss meant nothing.
I'd hate to think we nuked a perfectly nice world for nothing.
Hey, skipper. Seems like everything's coming together.
After what we saw on Virmire, it better come together.
Alenko-- the lieutenant. I'd hate to think his loss meant nothing.
If we get Udina on our side, he'll tell the Council to take a flying leap. If necessary.
How you holding up, skipper?
I hate being right.
Hey, Commander. Guess everything's gonna hit the fan soon, huh?
Commander.
Sure. I was hoping to get a minute of your time. Off the record.
Sure. I was just watching some mail from home.
All right? You mean, did you break my heart?
Just use, uh, protection. Tinfoil hat, maybe?
We've got a hard fight ahead.
You mean the rachni, right?
Kinda wish you'd got there sooner, Commander.
I keep an open-door policy. If you have any concerns, lay them on me.
It's not normal for an enlisted to speak informally with the commander.
Is this duty-related, Chief?
They may not serve the Alliance, Chief, but they're allies. At least as far as Saren goes.
He may not serve the Alliance, Chief, but he's an ally. At least as far as Saren goes.
You don't trust their motives because they're not human.
You don't trust his motives because he's not human.
Don't mince words, Chief. What's your concern?
You don't trust the Alliance's allies?
That's enough, Chief. You always second-guess your superiors?
I share your concerns, Chief. But I'm under orders.
I'm not going to lock them in sleeper pods for the whole trip, Williams.
I'm not going to lock him in a sleeper pod for the whole trip, Williams.
Standing up for ourselves doesn't mean standing alone.
I trust that's not insubordination I hear.
How do you get from "relying on ourselves" to "mistreating our allies?"
You've got a pessimistic view of the universe, Williams.
The Council's had a grudge against us since the First Contact War.
I don't see that as inevitable.
These seem like deeply-held beliefs, Williams. What made you think this way?
This is an Alliance warship, not the Parliament floor. If you're "Earth first," vote for the Terra Firma Party.
You sound like one of those Terra Firma Party pamphlets, Chief.
I come from a military family, too. My parents were both navy. Anybody in your family we might know?
I never knew my family. Grew up an orphan on Earth. Anybody in your family I'd have heard of?
You're lucky. I lost my family on Mindoir. Are you related to anyone I'd have heard of?
I don't think they meant to start a family tradition. But after sixteen years on ships and stations, how could I spend my life on the ground?
I saw a lot of people die. I can't sit back and let things like that happen.
Mainly, I wanted to serve. Protect the Alliance, save lives. You know.
No. The future of humanity is out here. There's so much we haven't seen yet.
Don't tell me you had Gunny Ellison. He's the only one who uses that word to describe shirking duty.
I'm here to put hypervelocity rounds through the heads of bad guys.
Earth's seen better days. Lots of pollution, too many people. People are trying to fix it, but...
It doesn't sound like you've worked with aliens before.
Guess you make a habit of second-guessing your superiors.
That's odd. Your record is spotless, and your technical scores are exemplary. You should be serving with the fleet.
I expect you to keep your family politics to yourself, Chief. This mission will be difficult enough without you picking fights with aliens.
All right. I can see where your concerns are coming from, Williams. But this is a multilateral mission. You're going to have to work with aliens, like it or not.
I don't think kissing turians will be necessary.
Would you kiss anyone I ordered you to?
I'm glad there won't be a problem.
Afraid I did.
We're in the middle of enemy territory, Chief. Don't you have better things to do than view mail from home?
I don't need to tell you it's inappropriate to gossip about how "cute" your commanding officer is.
Your sister, I assume?
I don't see how my personal life is any of your business, Chief.
I think I gave you the wrong impression.
Better than a commanding officer should with one of his crew.
We are. I'd like that to continue.
Liara? Why would you think that?
You think I'm interested in Liara because she's the only one I'm allowed to date?
Chief, should you be that casual with your commanding officer?
Your family seems to be important to you.
You have more than one sister? Sounds like a big family.
Did your father serve with the fleet?
Do you have a few minutes to talk, one-on-one?
Are you all right with Liara and I?
About Lieutenant Alenko. How are you holding up?
What's your opinion on the last mission?
We'll talk later, Williams.
Dismissed, Chief.
Of course.
Not for a personal chat.
What about?
Because they're not Alliance?
Because he's not Alliance?
Because they're aliens?
Because he's an alien?
What do you mean?
You don't trust aliens?
You're out of line!
My hands are tied.
I can't confine them.
I can't confine him.
We need allies.
Mind your words.
By mistrusting our allies?
How cynical.
Of course they will.
Not necessarily.
Why do you feel that?
Give me a break.
I've heard this before.
I understand your feelings.
Military family
Military family
Military family
Your service
Just shut up.
You have to work with aliens.
Yes.
I understand your feelings.
Damn right.
Wouldn't you?
I understand your feelings.
To serve the Alliance.
To see space.
For the action.
Wouldn't you?
I understand your feelings.
I understand your feelings.
"Goldbricking?"
I understand your feelings.
I understand your feelings.
I understand your feelings.
You deserve better.
Stuck groundside, huh?
Just one rotation?
I understand your feelings.
I understand your feelings.
Thanks.
What about me?
Remember that.
Good.
Sorry.
This isn't the time for mail.
That's unprofessional.
A relative?
Liara?
You're out of line.
Why's that?
I'm not interested in you.
And that was a problem.
Does that have to change?
That's cold.
Is that what you think?
Tell me about your family.
Mind your protocol.
I didn't mean to.
Sisters
Dad
Can we talk?
Liara and I.
About Kaidan
How are we doing?
Goodbye.
Goodbye.
Sorry. I forgot about your family situation.
Boom goes my promotion.
Ask me to clear a bunker of armed hostiles, no problem. Dealing with the foot in my mouth? Not so good with that.
Yeah. Military families, eh? With schedules like that, it's a wonder we ever have kids any more.
He was real proud when I made Chief. First thing he did was salute.
You must know what military wives are like. Strong because they have to be. Able to raise kids while Dad's away on a six-month cruise.
She has a degree in planetary geology. She and Dad both wanted to see new worlds.
She gave up her career to raise us, though.
All over. Same as you, I expect.
All over.
We transferred a half-dozen times before I finished grade school. You go where Personnel Command sends you, right?
I guess that's why I'm so tight with my sisters. We'd have to leave all our friends every two or three years.
Don't knock show tunes, sir. I might have to take exception.
Things were tense between Sarah and me for a while. Then we... bonded.
Dad always wanted to serve in space. But he wanted us to have real ground under our feet. He'd say, "Space is beautiful, but you can't raise a family there."
"I cannot rest from travel: I will drink life to the lees. All times I have enjoy'd greatly, have suffer'd greatly, both with those that loved me, and alone."
"For always roaming with a hungry heart. Much have I seen and known. Cities of men, and manners, climates, councils, governments..."
Just because I can drill you between the eyes at a hundred meters doesn't mean I can't like sensitive stuff.
Just don't spread it around.
Not everyone can bust up a slaver ring on their first tour, Commander.
Not everyone goes through the crap you had to, Commander.
Not everyone can win the Star of Terra, Commander.
Some of us just live ordinary lives.
Doubt it'll work on geth, sir, but I'll give it a shot.
Just like to remember why we fight.
"Ulysses" was Dad's favorite poem. Every time he shipped out, he recorded me reading it. He had a dozen versions when he retired.
He also brewed his own beer and played a mean baritone sax.
I sure hope so. I read it to his grave every time I go home.
Dad passed on a few years back. He's probably still watching, though.
So behave.
Dead on, skipper. He's with God now.
You know. From heaven. Wherever that is.
That's not a problem with you, is it? That I believe in God?
I'm glad you're open-minded about it.
Yeah. Guess you have.
I've met a few people who were really weirded out by my faith. Because I work in space, I can't believe in a higher power? Geez.
Hello? Have you people looked out the window? How can you look at this galaxy and not believe in something?
Commander, I'm not some kind of zealot. I believe in God. What everyone else believes is their business.
Just my commanding officer, huh? We'll have to see about that.
You should.
Mm. Too bad.
Me? I'm not saying anything, skipper.
I appreciate that, skipper.
I should double-check my gear before we move out. Those krogan aren't going to kill themselves.
I should get back to my duties. Didn't mean to take up so much of your time.
You're lucky to have a close family.
I'll be sure to mention your tact in your next performance review.
Or lack thereof. Relax, Williams. I've dealt with it.
I was an only child, but I get the idea. At least one of my parents was always on duty.
What about your mother? You haven't mentioned her.
Where did you grow up?
Next you'll tell me you all ran across green fields, singing show tunes.
After helping raise them, your sisters still talk to you? Amazing.
Sounds like your father wasn't around much. Wasn't your family stationed near him?
I never thought I'd hear you reciting poetry.
Is the rest of your life story this dull?
Poetry? You going to bore the enemy to death, marine?
I didn't know you liked classical literature.
He must have been a very boring man.
Does he still like it?
You mean from wherever we go after death.
He's not a zombie, is he?
I thought you said he was dead.
Everyone has the right to believe what they want. Says so in the Alliance charter. Only with fancier words.
You know that old saw, "there's never an atheist in a foxhole?" I've been in a lot of foxholes.
You start preaching in the CIC, we'll have a problem.
Your beliefs are your business. I'm your commanding officer, not your moral compass.
I'll look forward to our next talk.
We're on duty here, Williams.
What are you saying, Williams?
Must be nice.
Sounds familiar.
Mom
Home
Yes, charming.
You raised your sisters?
It's all right.
Yeah, tactful.
Forget it.
Your dad was gone a lot?
I've always liked that one.
You read poetry?
Bored now.
What's this crap?
Tennyson, right?
It's a good piece.
Sounds dull.
Really?
From the afterlife?
Yeah, sure he is.
Watching?
Of course not.
I do too.
Keep it to yourself.
Not my place to judge.
We will.
Keep it professional.
Oh?
Hey, skipper. Figured you'd be busy with tactical briefings and whatnot.
Don't know what I think about us attacking today, of all days. Kind of an ill omen.
Hey, skipper. Any interest in a small drink? It's a special occasion.
You're always on duty, Shepard.
I only have enough to toast the day, not the captain.
All right. But you know, a 'still is the first thing the engineers install after engines.
It's Armistice Day. When the First Contact War ended. My family always marks it.
Since I'm the only Williams aboard, I thought I'd ask you.
Maybe not. Maybe I'd rather share this with you. You ever consider that?
In our family, it's not really a celebration. More like an obligation.
Don't tell me you don't know about my family. My commanders always find out. It's not in my files or something?
There's a reason for the crap assignments.
I don't always play games, sir.
I'm General Williams' granddaughter. The commander of the Shanxi garrison in the War.
"The only human ever to surrender to an alien race."
"A Williams has to be better than the best, if only to avoid suspicion." That's what my Dad told me the night before he retired.
Cowardice. That's what the Terra Firma Party calls it.
Not formally. Dad got passed for promotion over and over. And I think my record merits more than garrison duty on a backwater agri colony.
It takes a special kind of thickheaded to march into a job where your family's blacklisted. I did it anyway.
I'm not going to let our name go down with Arnold and Quisling. Granddad deserved better than that.
The turians wrecked the orbitals in the first wave, and occupied the major cities. They sat in orbit, dropping rocks on anything that moved.
Granddad dispersed the troops. But when they went into the cities for supplies, the turians would wreck a block to eliminate one fire team.
Civilians were dying. His troops were starving. And he couldn't contact Alliance High Command. So he surrendered the garrison.
I'm on duty. Have anything without alcohol?
What's the occasion?
With all we've been through lately? Hell yes.
Last I checked, the Alliance Navy was dry.
You can't think I'm the most patriotic person on the ship.
Seems like an odd thing to celebrate. That was 26 years ago.
There's almost nothing in your files. Technical scores and a list of crap assignments.
Are you playing games with me?
I don't know what you're talking about.
I see. That's why you drive yourself so hard.
You're blacklisted because of your grandfather's cowardice.
Don't tell me you're blamed for that.
As I recall, your grandfather held out for a long time.
Non-alcoholic.
Occasion
Sure.
That's contraband.
I'm flattered.
Why me?
Why celebrate?
Your files are clean.
Spit it out.
What?
Now I understand.
I see.
Not your fault.
Shanxi
Would it make a difference? He's gone now. Dad's gone, too. And who would it impress? I'll never be good enough for the Alliance.
Look at who I am, Shepard. Do you ever hear me ask for help?
It's not that bad things don't happen to me. If you stay with me long enough, maybe I'll tell you about some of them. But I deal with them myself.
I don't need a shoulder to cry on, a knight to rescue me, or a man to make me happy. This is who I am. I like her. And you better like her, too.
He was relieved of command as soon as Shanxi was liberated. They brought him back to Earth in irons, but there was never a trial.
They quietly demoted him, and stuck him behind a desk. He retired a year later, and spent the rest of his life working construction in the colonies.
Sometimes we hear about attempts to get him exonerated in some official way. Nothing ever comes of them.
No, sir. I'd die to stop him, if that's what it takes.
Him, and anyone else who tries to screw with the Alliance.
If everyone else can look at Shanxi and say, "This is why humanity needs to be stronger," then so can I. I'm entitled.
So. You still interested in me? Baggage and all?
That's awful. Tell me you got that out of a fortune cookie.
Awfully smug, Shepard. What makes you think you can keep me in line?
Maybe I'm not. I guess you've been too busy saving the galaxy to think about it.
But hey, once we save the galaxy, maybe the Alliance will get its act together. Start acting like an actual government.
Have to disagree with you there, skipper. Giving aliens the run of our most advanced ship? Kowtowing to the Council?
The Council races will always think of themselves first. It's-- human nature. We can't afford to trust them. Not if the survival of humanity is on the line.
Shepard, I'm a soldier. You're my commander. If you give me an order, I'll follow it.
I thought you knew me better than that.
I'm a little complex, but I'm not some Freud-case.
I never intended to "undermine" you, Shepard. I believe in you. I wish you'd believe in anyone but yourself.
With your permission, sir, I'll return to my duties.
I don't know what God intends, Shepard.
I don't think humans have some divine mandate, if that's what you mean. I don't think we're superior.
That's-- Huh. I guess I never thought of it that way. All "big picture," I mean.
It doesn't make what happened to Granddad any better, though.
The brass will think I'm trading you favors for promotions. My favors don't come that cheap.
More than you know.
I have a feeling things will come to a head soon. But don't worry, Shepard. I'll protect you.
So now you know. Gonna kick me off the ship, skipper?
I also play a mean game of pool.
Just consider me a fire-and-forget missile.
Not to get all cheesy, but you're the first C.O. who's ever said that to me. Thanks, skipper.
He refused to sacrifice his men just to save face for humanity. You planning to throw yourself on a sword to save face for him?
I should have figured this out myself. I don't know how I can help you, though.
What happened to your grandfather after the war?
Sometimes you have to fight to the bitter end. You plan to bail if Saren gets the upper hand?
Is this why you're always going on about the Council?
Everyone comes with baggage, Ash. The trick is finding a matched set.
You're a difficult woman. Hard to read. Hard to keep in line.
You're interested in me? It's hard to tell.
The Alliance isn't perfect, but it does well enough.
The Alliance should be able to stand on its own. We can't. Yet. Why not learn from the races who have been standing for the last thousand years?
Whatever feelings I might have for you, we have to work with the Council. I can't let you second-guess our superiors.
I'm sorry. That was unfair. You never abused our relationship. Whatever it is. You're hard to figure out.
Seems like every time we run up against aliens, you whip out the "Earth first" card. I can't have my authority undermined.
Ash, you believe in God. An infallible, all-knowing creator with a plan for the universe. You think the diversity of views in the galaxy wasn't part of that?
Humans are aggressive. We think fast, we move fast. Wars have started because of our need for constant progress. The Council can balance that.
Humans are at their best when confronted with a problem. This crew proves that. Maybe the Council's opposition will inspire us to be better.
But you can't blame the Council for that, or the turians. It was our people who scapegoated him.
I'll pull strings to keep you under my command. I don't hold your family against you. You'll get what you deserve.
If not, we'll convince them. One way or the other, the Alliance is going to play a role in the Council.
We better get going, then. Seems I've got something to look forward to after we're done.
You're a valuable part of my crew, Williams. If I want an opinion "from the head," I go to Alenko. When I want one "from the heart," I go to you.
You're tough and decisive. I value those qualities.
You're part of the team, Williams. I don't care what your grandfather did or didn't do.
So do you.
How can I help?
Grandfather
He got what he deserved.
That's why you dislike aliens.
You deserve better.
Of course.
I like a challenge.
What about me?
The Alliance is all right.
They will.
Commence the saving.
It's not like that.
I've heard enough.
We can work with them.
I do.
Do I?
I'm just frustrated.
We need balance.
We need opposition.
The Council didn't do that.
Stay on the Normandy.
We need you.
You're valuable.
Of course not.
So what's up, Shepard?
The end of it, yeah. My family always marks it.
Just don't wave it around, skipper. Wrex might be hungry.
I'm the only Williams here. I guess you'd be the only other one interested in it.
That came out wrong. We may not always agree, but you get the job done for the Alliance.
How can you say that, given everything we've seen out here? They're already acting like Saren is our problem. Already siccing us on the bear.
Well. At least somebody knows that.
And a Star of Terra recipient, no less. Granddad must love that.
I thought you'd understand. You've had your back against the wall, too. You did what you had to.
You and he would have gotten along. He was a tough old bastard.
You have to do better than that to keep me by your side, Shepard.
I know. It's hard to be a patriot and pissed at the government, though. Who am I supposed to vote for?
I don't expect you to treat me differently from anyone else under your command. And if you have been -- quit it.
I'm sure Kirrahe wants to brief you. I should get out of your hair.
But anyway. I've got things to do before we land. I'm sure you do, too.
I hope we'll have some free time after all this is over.
You make me sound like some kind of math problem. Geez.
Heh. Yeah, you're right. I just hope-- Well, my sister Sarah always says, "Don't miss tomorrow for thinking about today." Smart kid. Not that I'd ever tell her that.
You're so dense. Sir.
Good luck, skipper. We have to convince the Council to act. No pressure.
You mean on the anniversary of the First Contact War?
Good thing I have my rabbit's foot. It should counteract all the negative waves.
I don't understand. What's today?
So you think my letting aliens on board was kowtowing to the Council?
We haven't been out here long, Ash. Once humanity has its space legs, we can start asserting ourselves.
We need to know what to expect out here. We've met aliens who oppose us, but don't want to destroy us. Maybe it's an opportunity to learn.
What happened to your grandfather shouldn't have happened.
I wish we'd had more free time. It may take me years to figure you out.
We'd be bored if we had any free time.
Free time for what?
Armistice Day.
Don't be superstitious.
Why today?
I'm interested.
I "kowtow?"
It's temporary.
We need to learn.
No, it doesn't.
We haven't had time to talk.
Don't bet on it.
What do you mean?
You're probably right. It still pisses me off.
You're an optimist, Shepard. I guess we'll have to consider this part of humanity's learning experience.
Don't start second-guessing yourself now. The Alliance needs you more than ever.
You're an optimist, skipper. Times like this, I'm glad I'm not.
Shepard, if you ever need to talk-- Hey, you listened to me bitch about my granddad.
You can talk to me, too. It's only fair, right?
Right. And why would anyone want to live with that? May as well just give up and wait for the Reapers, huh?
I've got equipment to check on.
If you get done with your "goldbricking," you just let me know.
Gunny Ellison'd be real disappointed if you give up now, Commander.
Commander.
Me too. What you said before, about the Council being part of God's plan? I'd love a peek at His map right now.
You know my feelings on the Council, skipper. I just can't believe Udina sold out the Alliance.
I was surprised Udina bought into it. I guess he's like any other politician.
The Council is used to being the biggest kid on the playground. They don't want to believe Daddy's coming to pick them up.
And eat them, I guess.
That's the spirit, skipper.
